    • primMST

      public List<Edge<E>> primMST()
      Uses the popular Prim's Algorithm to get the Minimum Spanning Tree of the graph, using a greedy, Dijkstra-like approach.
      Returns:
      the list of edges constructing the MST, or null if graph is disconnected.

    • kruskalMST

      public List<Edge<E>> kruskalMST()
      Uses Kruskal's Algorithm to get the Minimum Spanning Tree of the graph, using a sort-then-operate strategy that sorts edges by weight then taken the edges that combine two disconnected components together.
      Returns:
      the list of edges constructing the MST, or null if graph is disconnected.

    • dijkstra

      public Map<E,Integer> dijkstra(E source)
      Uses Dijkstra's Algorithm to find the shortest paths from a given source;
      Parameters:
      source - the origin of the search
      Returns:
      a Map of every node value with the length of its shortest path, or null in case of negative weights; a map entry value will be null if it's unreachable from source.

    • dagShortestPath

      public Map<E,Integer> dagShortestPath(E source)
      A shortest-path method that only operates on DAGs in O(V + E) relies on algorithmic invariance, processes the nodes in topological order and relaxes nodes to obtain the shortest path
      Parameters:
      source - the origin
      Returns:
      a Map of every node value with the length of its shortest path, a map entry value will be null if it's unreachable from source.

    • shuffleEdges

      public void shuffleEdges()
      Shuffles the edge list to randomize order and resets the sorted flag. Use this before benchmarking Kruskal to ensure fair comparison with unsorted edges.
